title: Locked Out
summary: A security script has locked everyone out of their own files. Can you get back into yours?
briefing:
Panic at DotTech's HR office. Last night the IT department ran a new "security script" on the computer dottech-hr. It removed **every** permission from the files in the home folders – nobody can read anything anymore. Not even their own files.

Your account was hit too. Your file `recovery_codes.txt` now just says `Permission denied`, and you need those codes.

Permissions decide what others may do with a file. But what can the **owner** of a file always do? Find out, and get back into your own file.
objective: Get back into your own file recovery_codes.txt and read the flag inside.
debrief:
You're back in! `ls -l` showed `----------`: no permissions at all. But the file was still **yours** – and the owner of a file may always change its permissions with `chmod`, whatever they are right now. `chmod 600` (or `chmod u+r`) gave you back the right to read it.

Did you try the HR payroll file too? `chmod` said `Operation not permitted`: it belongs to the user hr, and only the owner – or root – may change it. That is the rule that keeps other people's files safe.

The lesson for DotTech: permissions protect a file from **other** users, not from its owner or from root. Removing them all doesn't make anything more secure – it just breaks things. Use `chmod 600` for private files and `chmod 644` for files everyone may read.
hints: Look at the file's permissions and its owner. Permissions protect a file from other users – but the owner of a file can always change them.
`ls -l ~` shows the owner and the permissions. `chmod` changes them: `chmod u+r <file>` lets the owner read it, and `chmod 600 <file>` means "only the owner may read and write".
The flag is in `~/recovery_codes.txt`. Run `chmod 600 ~/recovery_codes.txt`, then `cat ~/recovery_codes.txt`.

mails.subject: Nobody can open anything!
mails.body:
Hi, Priya from HR. Last night IT ran a new "security script" on dottech-hr, and now NOBODY can open their own files. Not even me.

Your account was hit too – your recovery codes are in there. Can you find a way back in? Mission: **Locked Out**.

Priya

mails.subject: Re: Nobody can open anything!
mails.body:
You did it! And you explained `chmod` so well that half the office has fixed their own files.

IT has been asked, politely, to never run that script again.

Priya
